domains.title: She-Who-Invites
domains.subtitle: Creator Goddess, Mother of Kami, Queen of Yomi
domains.lead: Izanami is the female half of the primordial creator pair and the first being to die. Her body became the landscape of the underworld, and her vengeful pursuit of Izanagi established the boundary between the living and the dead. She is both the mother of the gods and the fearsome ruler of Yomi.

cards.name: Creator Goddess

cards.name: Mother of Kami

cards.name: Death in Childbirth

cards.name: Queen of Yomi

mythology.lead: Izanami's mythology is central to Japanese understandings of creation, death, and the separation between the living and the dead.

myths.title: The Creation of the Islands
myths.text: Standing on the Floating Bridge of Heaven, Izanami and Izanagi stirred the primordial ocean with the jeweled spear. When they lifted it, brine dripped and congealed into the first island. They descended and, after a failed first marriage ceremony caused by Izanami speaking first, properly created the Japanese archipelago.

myths.title: Death in Childbirth
myths.text: Izanami gave birth to the fire god Kagutsuchi, whose flames burned her so severely that she died. From her dying body came further kami: the mountains, rivers, and earth. Her death introduced mortality into the world and sent Izanagi on his grief-stricken journey to Yomi.

myths.title: The Queen of Yomi
myths.text: In the underworld, Izanami was consumed by decay and rage. When Izanagi broke his promise not to look at her, she pursued him to the boundary of Yomi and cursed him: she would kill one thousand people each day. Izanagi replied that he would cause one thousand five hundred to be born. This exchange established the endless traffic between life and death.

lore.syncretism: Izanami has parallels with underworld goddesses across Eurasia, but her specific role as the first mother who dies in childbirth and becomes the queen of death is distinctively Japanese. She is venerated at shrines associated with the underworld and with safe childbirth, embodying the thin boundary between birth and death.
lore.culturalLegacy: Izanami remains a powerful figure in Japanese religious imagination. She appears in literature, manga, anime, and video games as both a tragic mother and a terrifying underworld queen. Her story shapes rituals around death, pollution, and purification in Shinto.
lore.extendedMeditation: Izanami is the first separation. Her death created the underworld, and her curse set the rhythm of mortality. To remember her is to remember that life and death are not opposites but phases of a single story, and that the one who gives birth may also become the one who receives the dead.
lore.archaeology: Izanami is worshipped at shrines associated with the creation pair, such as Taga Taisha in Ōmi and Izanami Jinja on Awaji Island, traditionally identified as the first island created by the divine couple. These sites preserve shrine architecture and ritual traditions connected to the creation myth.
